stem: In periodontal disease progression, what happens to the junctional epithelium as subgingival plaque extends onto the root surface?
options: It detaches completely and disappears
It proliferates apically on the root surface while a strand always remains at the base of the pocket
It converts into connective tissue attachment
It becomes keratinized and resistant to bacterial invasion
justification: The text explains that the junctional epithelium enables it to proliferate apically on the root surface, and a strand of junctional epithelium will always be present at the base of the advancing pocket, denying the bacteria access to the connective tissues in this direction.

stem: What is the definition of occlusal trauma (trauma from occlusion) as described in periodontal texts?
options: Loss of tooth structure due to erosion
An injury to any part of the masticatory system resulting from abnormal occlusal contact relationships
Inflammation of the gingiva caused by plaque accumulation
A fracture of the alveolar bone from external trauma
justification: Occlusal trauma is defined as an injury to any part of the masticatory system resulting from abnormal occlusal contact relationships, as stated in the chapter on occlusal trauma.

stem: According to the discussion of mucogingival assessment, why are lip-pull tests considered unreliable for assessing the need for mucogingival surgery?
options: They cause excessive bleeding of the gingival margin
Manipulation of lip and cheek in this way is not physiological and such tests are meaningless
They can only be performed under general anaesthesia
They are accurate only in edentulous patients
justification: The text states that manipulation of lip and cheek in this way is not physiological and such tests are, therefore, meaningless, referring to lip-pull tests for mucogingival assessment.

stem: What is described as an essential factor in establishing a pattern of behaviour that makes a patient independent of professional support during oral hygiene instruction?
options: Motivation
Sedation
Antibiotic prophylaxis
Radiographic monitoring
justification: The text states that motivation is an essential factor in establishing a pattern of behaviour which will make the patient independent of professional support, in the context of dental health education.

stem: Besides allowing access for scaling and root planing, what other objective should the surgical technique selected in periodontal treatment planning achieve?
options: Complete removal of the alveolar bone
A gingival contour which allows plaque control afterwards and is acceptable cosmetically
Elimination of the need for post-operative home care
Permanent widening of the periodontal ligament space
justification: The text notes the surgical technique should allow access for scaling and root planing at the time of surgery but also result in a gingival contour which will allow plaque control afterwards and be acceptable cosmetically.

stem: According to the text, what is fundamental to the success of all aspects of periodontal treatment?
options: Effective scaling and root planing
Systemic antibiotic therapy
Orthodontic realignment of teeth
Occlusal adjustment alone
justification: The chapter states that effective scaling and root planing is fundamental to the success of all aspects of periodontal treatment, and expertise in this field is essential.

stem: Which surgical procedure is described simply as 'the removal of unwanted gingival tissue'?
options: Flap procedure
Mucogingival surgery
Gingivectomy
Osteoplasty
justification: The text lists gingivectomy as simply the removal of unwanted gingival tissue, distinguishing it from flap procedures and mucogingival surgery.

stem: In the management of a thickened palatal flap margin during molar periodontitis surgery, what procedure is carried out before the palatal gingivectomy?
options: Root resection
Osteoplasty has been carried out
Free gingival grafting
Coronal repositioning of the flap
justification: The figure legend describes that osteoplasty has been carried out prior to palatal gingivectomy to allow better flap adaptation to tooth and bone.

stem: Why are approximal surfaces of posterior teeth with large restorations especially susceptible to periodontal problems near overhanging margins?
options: Because they are more likely to have overhanging margins, especially if matrix bands are used without adequate wedging
Because they are always placed subgingivally by design
Because composite resin is inherently more plaque-retentive than amalgam
Because they require no interproximal contact
justification: The text explains that late diagnosis of caries results in large restorations which are more likely to have overhanging margins, especially if matrix bands are used without adequate wedging.

stem: What does Ante's Law propose regarding fixed bridgework in cases of reduced periodontal support?
options: The number of pontics should never exceed two
The root surface area of the abutment teeth should be equal to or greater than the root surface area of the teeth to be replaced by pontics
Only anterior teeth may serve as abutments
Bridges must always be cantilevered from a single abutment
justification: The text states that Ante proposed that in a fixed bridge the root surface area of the abutment teeth should be equal to or greater than the root surface area of the teeth to be replaced by pontics.

stem: How is desquamative gingivitis characterized clinically?
options: A localized abscess with purulent discharge
A painful gingival lesion with a smooth, red, glistening surface with a tendency to desquamation and haemorrhage on slight trauma
A firm, fibrotic enlargement of the gingiva with no bleeding tendency
A pigmented lesion confined to the attached gingiva
justification: Desquamative gingivitis is described as a painful gingival lesion or lesions characterised by a smooth, red, glistening surface with a tendency to desquamation and haemorrhage on slight trauma.

stem: Which periodontal pathogens is tetracycline noted to be particularly effective against, given that its concentrations in gingival crevicular fluid are higher than in serum?
options: Streptococcus mutans and Lactobacillus species
A. actinomycetemcomitans and Capnocytophaga
Candida albicans and Actinomyces israelii
Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa
justification: The text states tetracycline is a broad-spectrum bacteriostatic antibiotic, effective against the majority of periodontal pathogens and notably against A. actinomycetemcomitans and Capnocytophaga.

stem: Why is monitoring of attachment levels considered of little value once a maintenance programme is achieving a physiological gingival sulcus?
options: Because attachment loss is difficult and time consuming to measure, involving identification of the amelocemental junction and pocket base
Because attachment levels are unrelated to periodontal health
Because periodontal probes cannot detect the amelocemental junction
Because attachment loss occurs regardless of maintenance quality
justification: The text explains that attachment loss will not occur when maintenance is sufficient, and there is little point in monitoring since attachment loss is difficult and time consuming to measure since it involves identification of the amelocemental junction as well as the base of the pocket.

stem: What is recommended for the local treatment of severe cases of acute necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis when only loose debris removal is possible?
options: Immediate surgical flap debridement
Removing loose debris with cotton wool pellets soaked in hydrogen peroxide
Application of a chlorhexidine varnish only
Extraction of all affected teeth
justification: The text states that in severe cases it may only be possible to remove loose debris with cotton wool pellets soaked in hydrogen peroxide, which is probably effective in the local treatment described.

stem: What is described as the basis for conventional, mechanical treatment of periodontitis regarding plaque ecology?
options: Eliminating all subgingival bacteria permanently through antibiotics
Maintaining a plaque ecology unfavourable for virulent species by removing subgingival plaque and keeping supragingival plaque and gingivitis at a minimum
Sealing the gingival sulcus with a periodontal dressing
Applying fluoride varnish to root surfaces monthly
justification: The text states that the way to achieve a permanent reduction of the most virulent species is to maintain a plaque ecology unfavourable for these species, by removing subgingival plaque and keeping supragingival plaque and gingivitis at a minimum, forming the basis for conventional mechanical treatment.
